subject.title: Feature: Respect userTimezone in memory file timestamps and naming

question: Should bundled session-memory artifacts switch from host-local filename/header timestamps to `agents.defaults.userTimezone`, or remain host-local as currently documented?
rationale: Current shipped code and docs make host-local session-memory behavior explicit, while adjacent memory-flush code already follows configured user timezone, so automation cannot safely choose compatibility versus consistency.

options.title: Adopt userTimezone for session-memory
options.body: Update the bundled handler, focused tests, and docs to use resolved `agents.defaults.userTimezone` for filenames and headers while accepting the artifact naming change.

options.title: Keep host-local session-memory
options.body: Document that bundled session-memory remains host-local and limit this issue to the already-aligned pre-compaction memory flush behavior.

options.title: Design an explicit memory timezone knob
options.body: Add a dedicated config surface only if maintainers want per-memory behavior separate from both host local time and `userTimezone`.

recommendation.title: Adopt userTimezone for session-memory
recommendation.body: Update the bundled handler, focused tests, and docs to use resolved `agents.defaults.userTimezone` for filenames and headers while accepting the artifact naming change.

likelyOwner.reason: The open question is product/config semantics around the shared time contract, and this person is the strongest adjacent history signal for date-time and memory-core boundaries.
